scope: Independent read-only native snapshot/publish lock-chain check; reported to parent agent, with four source hashes independently checked against signed source ed925cc1.
conclusions: HostBridge.snapshot takes and releases phone snapshot lock first, then enters adapter monitor and Wi-Fi lock. Wi-Fi threads do not acquire adapter, phone or roomLock in reverse order.
Snapshot loops only two seats and nine keys, constructs JSON and consumes cached pulses; it performs no UI callback, network I/O, wait or join.
START changes the existing start/buttons[4] state. Snapshot polling is the same before and after game phase changes; there is no native START-specific scene or phase wait.
HostBridge.publish validates a bounded string and LanGameServer.publish parses/re-encodes JSON then assigns volatile published. It does not acquire roomLock or write the network.
Periodic broadcast uses worker threads, copies peers then releases the phone lock before socket writes.
TCP START/long_press/release state updates are within short locks; ACK sending is outside the lock and does not wait for WebView or JS phase.
conclusion: No definite START-specific native deadlock or blocking defect was found. This does not identify or rule out an unrecorded Android/emulator failure.
